chunks.arabic_text: الْخَصَائِصُ: ابْنُ مَسْرُورٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَامِرٍ، عَنْ عَمِّهِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ صُهَيْبٍ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Khasa'is: Ibn Masrur, from Ibn A'mir, from his uncle Abdallah, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Suhayb who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يَقُولُ: لَا يَجْمَعُ اللَّهُ لِمُنَافِقٍ وَلَا فَاسِقٍ حُسْنَ السَّمْتِ وَالْفِقْهِ وَحُسْنَ الْخُلُقِ أَبَدًا

translations.en: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Allah never grants the hypocrite or the corrupt sinner goodness of conduct, understanding, and goodness of character together.

en.summary: The Imam (peace be upon him) states that Allah does not combine three specific virtues—goodness of demeanor (husn al-samt), religious understanding (fiqh), and good character (husn al-kulq)—in a single person who is a hypocrite (munafiq) or a corrupt sinner (fasiq). This highlights that while these individuals may possess some traits, the complete combination of these spiritual and intellectual qualities is reserved for the sincere and upright.
en.seo_question: What three qualities does Allah not combine in a hypocrite or corrupt sinner?
